models._note: Per-stage model and effort. ENFORCED only where a fresh context begins - a subagent with frontmatter. Stages that run in your session inherit the session model whatever this file says; for those this block is a recommendation the skill reads out so you can choose before the stage runs. Values: model = inherit | cheap | <model id>. effort = inherit | low | medium | high. See references/models.md.

import.why: inferring requirements from code you have never read is the hardest inference in the lifecycle, and every mistake becomes a requirement someone later confirms

intake.why: contradiction detection against the whole spec is the hardest call here, and a missed contradiction merges silently

tests.why: runs in your session against a written plan

evals.why: mechanical pass/fail, 20-50 of them nightly - this is where cost lives

checks.why: NO MODEL IN THIS PATH. Stage 5 runs declared scripts and compares coverage; a model deciding whether a check passed is the failure the stage exists to prevent

review.why: fresh context, adversarial, low volume - the one place raising effort is cheap and clearly worth it

document.why: reads the whole active spec and maps every section to ids; cheap models drop the mapping and write plausible prose

announce.why: every claim has to trace to a merged PR or a requirement id, and this is the one artifact that leaves the building

diagnose.why: 2 sigma is summarising; raise it for 3 sigma, which proposes a change

models._advisor_note: advisor = null | <model alias or id>. Optional; null or absent means no advisor. When set, the unattended CI build (templates/build-from-spec.yml) passes it to Claude Code as --advisor <model>: a second model the build agent MAY consult, sent the whole transcript, billed at its own rates. Advice, never a gate - the agent decides whether and when to call it, and no check relies on it. Anything but a model name (a letter or digit, then letters, digits and . _ : @ -) refuses the run. The pairing with the build model is checked by Claude Code, not here. See references/models.md, The advisor.
models._build_caps_note: build_caps caps the unattended CI build (templates/build-from-spec.yml) and nothing else: max_turns = null | <whole number 1-999999>, the agentic turns Claude Code may take, passed as --max-turns; max_budget_usd = null | <US dollars above 0, in whole cents, below 1000000>, the spend it may reach by its own client-side estimate, passed as --max-budget-usd. Never uncapped: null or absent takes the built-in default, 100 turns and 20.00 dollars, and prepare says so; any other value - a string, zero, a negative, a fraction of a turn or of a cent - refuses the run before a model is called. Claude Code stops the run at whichever cap it reaches, the job fails and no pull request is opened; the spend can pass its cap by the response that crosses it. The job's timeout-minutes is the third stop. Scheduled prompts get no cap from here. See references/ci-build.md, The caps.

bands._note: The scheduled band check executes detection_command from HERE, never a path read out of bands.yaml. Two sources must agree: this binding and the literal frozen into the scheduled prompt when a human installed it.

band_bindings._note: One binding per band added beside `bands` above, each with its own bands file and its own scheduled task (templates/scheduled-band-metric.md, taskId sdlc-bands-<slug>-<metric>), which runs detection_command from HERE only when it matches the literal frozen into that task. `bands` and the task installed from it are untouched, so what that task runs does not change. Each command prints a `tier:` line the task acts on. See references/stage-9-maintain.md.

jira._note: Identifiers only — JIRA_API_TOKEN stays in the environment. Writes are append-only: a comment, a remote link, a label, or a transition named in `transitions`. The description is written once at creation and never edited, and no requirement text is ever written back — the spec's authority comes from being committed and diffable, and a copy in a description any Jira user can edit is a second spec that disagrees invisibly. `create_for_channels` must never list `jira_issue`: that intent already has a ticket, and a second one splits the audit trail. `transition_on` is the subset of `transitions` that actually moves the ticket; `test` is deliberately absent. A transition name missing from the project's workflow is reported, never approximated, and ids are looked up per workflow rather than stored here. Labels use hyphens because a Jira label may not contain a space. `on_failure` has one legal value — the repo is the source of truth and Jira is a view, so every Jira error is reported and none blocks a stage.

status_map._note:
Jira workflow state -> backlog status. Declared once so two boards do not resolve the same state differently. Read only: nothing here is ever written back to Jira.

UNVERIFIED AGAINST ANY LIVE JIRA. As of 2026-09-06 not one of these eleven mappings has been run against a real instance. They were checked on that date against Atlassian's own published documentation and nothing else, and that check found three things to act on before trusting this block. Edit it against YOUR project before you rely on it.

1. STATUS NAMES ARE PER PROJECT, SO NO FIXED LIST IS RIGHT EVERYWHERE. Atlassian's Jira Cloud platform OpenAPI (developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json, retrieved 2026-09-06) documents GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/statuses as "Returns the valid statuses for a project. The statuses are grouped by issue type, as each project has a set of valid issue types and each issue type has a set of valid statuses.", scopes a status PROJECT or GLOBAL, and lets StatusCreate take any name up to 255 characters. Read your project's own statuses and rewrite the keys below to match.

2. ONLY THE CATEGORY IS STABLE ACROSS INSTANCES, AND THERE ARE EXACTLY THREE. "All statuses, even custom statuses you create yourself, must belong to one of three status categories - To do, In progress, or Done." (support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/what-is-a-workflow-status/, retrieved 2026-09-06). The same OpenAPI types statusCategory as a closed enum, TODO | IN_PROGRESS | DONE. Three categories cannot express `blocked` or `long-term`, which is the only reason this map keys on names at all. So: a name that is not listed below is NOT unknown - fall back to its category, TODO -> todo, IN_PROGRESS -> in-progress, DONE -> done, and say on the row that the fallback was used.

3. WHAT THE ELEVEN ACTUALLY ARE, measured 2026-09-06 against support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/what-are-issue-statuses-priorities-and-resolutions/. SEVEN are named there as statuses Jira ships by default: To Do, Backlog, Selected for Development, In Progress, In Review, Done, Closed. THREE appear nowhere on that page and were invented here as plausible team conventions - In Dev, Blocked, On Hold. They are kept because an admin may create any of them, not because Jira supplies them. ONE is a category error: that page lists "Won't do" among RESOLUTIONS, not statuses, and spells it with a lower-case d - so this row matches nothing unless someone has separately made a status of that name. Matching here is exact-string, and Atlassian's own pages spell one state both "In Progress" and "In progress", so assume the casing below is wrong until you have read the project's statuses.

plan_page._note: plan_page themes the plan page (scripts/build-plan-page.sh) and nothing else. stylesheet = null | <path to a CSS file in this repository>: the page takes its colours and fonts from the custom properties that file sets on :root (light) and on :root under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), [data-theme="dark"] or .dark (dark), and only values of a colour or font-name shape; url(), @import and anything that is not a colour or a font list are never taken. tokens = {} | {<page token>: "--<property>"}: names the property for a page token (bg, surface, text, muted, border, accent, accent-text, font, mono) when it is not one of the documented names. null, a file that cannot be read, one outside the repository or one that sets nothing usable gives the built-in theme, and the page says which - never an error. A font is named, never loaded. See references/plan-page.md, The project's own look.
